verified.reason: Independently reproduced: tapsign.newRequest/do set X-LC-Id/X-LC-Key and (when session != "") X-LC-Session (tapsign/client.go:114-115,124-126); taptapoauth.fetchAccount sets Authorization (taptapoauth/client.go:195). NewService/newClient only require a non-nil Doer and never set CheckRedirect (tapsign/service.go:52-62, taptapoauth/service.go:44-51). Go 1.27.1 net/http (C:\Program Files\Go\src\net\http\client.go:820-841,1017-1039) treats only Authorization/Www-Authenticate/Cookie/Cookie2/Proxy-Authorization/Proxy-Authenticate as sensitive; every other header, including X-LC-*, is copied from the initial request to every redirect hop. An empirical probe (httptest redirector -> target with a plain &http.Client{}) showed X-LC-Id/X-LC-Key/X-LC-Session replayed across a 127.0.0.1 -> localhost (cross-domain) hop, while Authorization was stripped on that hop and kept on a same-host hop. So the claim is exactly right. In-repo the sole wiring (cmd/referencesource/main.go:163-166) sets httpclient.NoCrossHostRedirects, and httpclient.Retry preserves the wrapped *http.Client, so the deployed path is safe; medium (not high) is correct because exploitation now requires an out-of-repo caller or a future wiring that passes a plain/DNS-resolving client.
verified.evidence_checked: tapsign/client.go:114-115,124-126; taptapoauth/client.go:195; tapsign/service.go:52-62; taptapoauth/service.go:44-51; cmd/referencesource/main.go:163-166; httpclient/retry.go:112-131; net/http/client.go:820-841,1017-1039; empirical probe _audit/round9/verify/s07probe

verified.reason: Code order verified: vault.Enroll calls s.repo.Put at service.go:245-258, then s.record at 259-267; on audit failure it returns the bare audit error with no repo.Delete/rollback, whereas Use audits before handing over plaintext (service.go:334-339). The audit.Logger contract is synchronous and returns errors (audit/audit.go:35-39), and the Postgres sink really can fail (internal/store/postgres/auditbatch.go:68-69,195, errAuditDrainExpired/errAuditClosed). The federation path is exactly as described: storeBindingSecret -> vault.Enroll (internal/federation/binding.go:81-94); bind.go:192-197 returns immediately on that error, so the rollback at bind.go:198-215 (which runs only when bindings.Put fails) is skipped, leaving an encrypted upstream token with no binding row and no audit event. One correction that does not change severity: the residue is not absolutely unreachable — a later re-bind of the same (user, game, source) overwrites the record via Enroll, and DeleteSubject clears it — so bind.go's 'only an account erasure would clear' comment overstates it. Confirmed medium (reliability/data-integrity, unaudited secret at rest during an audit outage).

Behaviour and complexity verified: MemoryRepo.ListPage ignores its ctx, calls r.List (repo.go:233), and List materialises and deep-clones every record (WrappedDEK/Nonce/Ciphertext/Meta via cloneRecord) and sorts N identities under an RLock (repo.go:202-217). ListPage is the RecordPager path Rotate takes (rotate.go:42-60) with rotatePageSize=200 (rotate.go:96), so a full rotation is ceil(N/200) whole-store passes: O(N^2/200) clones and O(N^2 log N /200) comparisons. Call-frequency reasoning reduces the impact but not the defect: the only production caller is the operator-run startup action -rotate-keys (cmd/re0auth/main.go:442-443,1204-1205); it is not on any request path. The memory driver is selectable (cmd/re0auth/config.go:686-691, cmd/re0auth/main.go:897), which is the only way this is reachable. Confirmed low.

The code divergence is real: Enroll seals under bindingAAD(recordVersion, id.Subject, id.Provider) (service.go:224), Use derives the AAD from the caller's id (service.go:300) while Rotate derives it from rec.Identity (rotate.go:104). But it is not reachable with any shipped Repo: MemoryRepo.Get and Postgres Vault.Get are keyed by the exact (subject, provider), so the returned Record.Identity always equals the requested id. Triggering it requires a third-party Repo implementation that returns a record for a different identity — i.e. a bug in code outside this repository — and even then the consequence is fail-closed (Use rejects the swapped ciphertext with an unwrap/decrypt error) plus a confusing signal, not a credential compromise. Overstated as a low production defect; retained as an API-robustness note (reject rec.Identity != id).

Verified literally: data.Interval/data.ExpiresIn are untrusted int64 JSON fields multiplied by time.Second with only a <= 0 fallback (taptapoauth/client.go:81-103). For Interval=9223372036 the product is 9.223372036e18 ns (positive, ~292 years, just under MaxInt64), so no overflow guard is needed to produce an effectively infinite poll interval; larger values wrap negative and are silently replaced by defaults. The consumer is real: referencesource/taptap.go:149-160 uses ExpiresAt to expire attempts and auth.Interval for nextPoll and RetryAfterSeconds. Only the configured TapTap token endpoint (compromised/buggy/DNS-hijacked) controls the values, so low is appropriate.

Verified: tapsign.client.Verify sends the decrypted session token upstream (client.go:44-48) and never calls c.finish/audit.Record, unlike Rotate/Revoke/Redeem (client.go:62,74,149,171,197-211). Verify is part of the exported Service interface (tapsign/service.go:31-34) and the package documents itself as a reusable capability, so any consumer that probes credential health produces a credential use with no audit trail. Note for severity: no in-repo production caller exists today (only tests), so the practical exposure is a library-invariant gap rather than a live leak; low stands because the package is an exported API whose other methods all audit.

boundDetail does only replace \r/\n and cap runes (taptapoauth/client.go:337-343), so ESC/NUL/other C0 bytes survive in the error string — that code behaviour is confirmed. The stated impact, however, does not follow on any reachable in-repo sink: the only production propagation of these errors is referencesource/taptap.go:210-226, which JSON-encodes them (Go's encoding/json escapes control characters as \uXXXX), and there is no production code that logs err.Error() from taptapoauth (grepped). The log/terminal-forgery scenario therefore needs an out-of-repo caller with a raw sink; completeness hardening only, not a low production defect.
verified.evidence_checked: taptapoauth/client.go:314-343; referencesource/taptap.go:210-226; grep for err.Error() in production code

verified.reason: The unguarded dereferences are real (tapsign/client.go:44-48,178,224-227 call drain(resp)/resp.StatusCode after only an err check; taptapoauth/client.go:202,239 close resp.Body with no nil check), and they contrast with httpclient's own guarded drain (httpclient/retry.go:195-201) and Bulkhead's resp.Body==nil branch (httpclient/outbound.go:225-228). But the precondition is an injected Doer that violates the *http.Client contract (Do guarantees a non-nil Response and non-nil Body when err == nil), and every in-repo wiring uses *http.Client or httpclient.Retry over it, which can never return (nil, nil) or a nil Body. A nil-returning Doer is defective operator-supplied code, not attacker-reachable; downgraded to info as defensive-hardening.

The overwrite is real: Enroll always sets CreatedAt: now (service.go:244-254) and Repo.Put replaces wholesale, with the Postgres adapter doing created_at = EXCLUDED.created_at (internal/store/postgres/vault.go:112-120). But the stated impact is unsupported: no production code reads vault.Record.CreatedAt. The operator/account views the finding cites use account.User.CreatedAt and oauth-client CreatedAt (internal/httpapi/admin_routes.go:48, export_routes.go:84 uses accounts.GetUser, not the vault); the only consumers of vault List/Get are rotation and federation token use, neither of which touches CreatedAt. So it is a latent data-semantics loss, not a current correctness defect; becomes low if any consumer is added.
verified.evidence_checked: vault/service.go:244-254; internal/store/postgres/vault.go:109-124; internal/httpapi/export_routes.go:64-84; internal/httpapi/admin_routes.go:25,48; grep for vault Record.CreatedAt consumers

verified.reason: Verified: rotate() invalidates the old token upstream and returns the replacement (tapsign/client.go:79-107); Rotate then performs the audit and returns (next, finish(...)) (client.go:60-63), and finish returns a non-nil error when the audit fails even though the rotation succeeded (client.go:197-211). So the caller receives a replacement credential together with a non-nil error, and the idiomatic 'if err != nil { return err }' discards the only live token; a retry with the dead old token yields ErrInvalidCredential and cannot converge. Revoke (client.go:65-75) has the safer mirror shape. Note for severity: no in-repo production caller of Rotate exists (only tests), so this is an exported-API hazard rather than a live outage; low stands because the package is a reusable service interface and the failure mode is a permanent logout.

The uint32 truncation described exists (vault/envelope.go:148,150), but it is unreachable: subject/provider would each have to exceed 4 GiB, which would exhaust memory before any store accepted it, and the layout truncation is explicitly documented in the code. The finding already grades it info/no-change; confirmation only records that the code matches the description.

summary: S07: 11 findings verified by re-reading every cited site plus callers, stdlib source and one empirical repro. CONFIRMED 7: S07-1 medium (cross-host redirect replays X-LC-* headers; empirically reproduced on go1.27.1; in-repo caller mitigates, so medium), S07-2 medium (Enroll stores before auditing; federation then aborts before bindings.Put, leaving an encrypted unaudited token), S07-3 low (MemoryRepo.ListPage is O(N) per page, making -rotate-keys O(N^2/200); operator-only path), S07-5 low (unbounded/overflowing interval and expires_in), S07-6 low (exported Verify audits nothing while all peer methods do), S07-10 low (Rotate returns the replacement token with a non-nil audit error), S07-11 info (dead uint32 length truncation). DOWNGRADED 4, all to info for overstated reachability: S07-4 (needs a third-party Repo returning a mismatched identity; shipped repos cannot), S07-7 (control chars survive boundDetail but no in-repo sink logs the raw error; HTTP answers JSON-escape), S07-8 (nil-Response deref needs a Doer that violates the *http.Client contract; in-repo Doers cannot), S07-9 (Enroll overwrites CreatedAt, but no production code reads vault Record.CreatedAt). REJECTED 0. No new severe finding was invented. Discovery totals (0 critical, 0 high, 2 medium, 8 low) overstate four low items by one notch; severity of every reachable finding was otherwise upheld.
